data.title: Wrangler expands brand with new footwear line from Genesco
data.description:
Wrangler is extending its brand into a footwear line through licensing partner Genesco with its Fall 2026 collection that features western-style footwear for men, women, and children.

The Wrangler footwear line launches September 15 on the company’s website, with availability at select U.S. retailers rolling out later in the season.

“We’ve combined Wrangler’s iconic heritage and deep connection with consumers with our footwear expertise to create a collection that is unmistakably Wrangler,” said Rick Higgins, president of Genesco Brands Group.

Wrangler, a primary brand of Kontoor Brands , is riding the coattails of a fashion renaissance in Western wear thanks to the popularity of shows like Yellowstone, the proliferation of country music festivals, and brand ambassadors that include Lainey Wilson and Cody Johnson. Wrangler’s affordability (ranging from $25 to $50), improved fit, and expanded women’s line helped fuel Q2 sales and an upbeat outlook for the remainder of the year.

During Kontoor Brands’ second quarter earnings call, CEO Scott Baxter acknowledged the strength of the brand and its growing popularity with both men and women.

“Western sits at the heart of Wrangler's DNA, and we have never been stronger. To support this momentum, we will continue to invest behind our product innovation and demand creation platforms to solidify our position as the authority in the category,” Baxter said.

data.title: Crypto Stocks Slide Ahead of Clarity Act Vote
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Crypto stocks are trading lower, ahead of a key procedural vote the Senate is set to hold on the Clarity Act, which would represent the first regulatory framework expected to usher in wider acceptance of crypto.

Shares of Circle Internet fell 8.2%, to $89.39, on Tuesday. At the same time, Coinbase shares were down 6.7%, to $178.72, and Strategy shares were off 5%, to $130.05.

Shares of Riot Platforms were down 4.2%, to $20.08. Robinhood shares were recently trading 3.7% lower, at $110.14, while MARA Holdings shares declined 2.6%, to $11.20.

The legislation faces several challenges, including disagreements over ethics language that would prevent government officials from profiting off digital assets, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Write to Connor Hart at connor.hart@wsj.com

data.title: REG - Borders & Southern - Exercise of Warrants
data.description:
RNS Number : 8846U Borders & Southern Petroleum plc 15 September 2026  

15 September 2026

Borders & Southern Petroleum plc

("Borders & Southern" or the "Company")

Exercise of Warrants

Borders & Southern Petroleum plc (AIM: BOR), the London based independent oil and gas exploration company with appraisal and exploration assets offshore the Falkland Islands, announces that it has received notification from a warrant holder to exercise warrants over 251,600 new ordinary shares of 1 pence each in the capital of the Company ("Warrant Shares") at the exercise price of 10 pence per Warrant Share, for an aggregate cash value of £25,160.

Application has been made for admission of the Warrant Shares to trading on AIM ("Admission") and it is expected that Admission will occur on or around 22 September 2026. The Warrant Shares will rank pari passu with the existing ordinary shares of 1 pence each in the capital of the Company (“Ordinary Shares”).

The balance of the warrants expire on September 21 unless exercised before that date.

Total Voting Rights

Following Admission, the total issued share capital of the Company will consist of 886,571,382 Ordinary Shares with voting rights. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in treasury. Therefore, the total number of voting rights in the Company will be 886,571,382 and this is the figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change in their interest in, the share capital of the Company under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

data.title: Masco Names Yaron Ben David Chief Technology And AI Officer
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - U.S. home-improvement products maker Masco Corp. (MAS), on Tuesday announced the appointment of Yaron Ben David as Chief Technology and AI officer, effective September 15, 2026, a newly created role reflecting the company's push to expand its technology and artificial intelligence capabilities.

Ben David will report to CEO Jon Nudi and join Masco's executive committee. The company said the role brings enterprise technology, data and AI under one leader to help scale innovation, boost productivity and create value across its brands.

Yaron Ben David previously served as chief digital officer at Standard Industries, leading AI, data, cybersecurity and digital transformation initiatives. He also held senior leadership positions in Israel's Unit 8200, the Israel Defense Forces' intelligence and cyber organization.

On the NYSE, shares of Masco are currently losing 1.38 percent, changing hands at $68.45.

data.title: ICE Canada Morning Comment: Canola Pulling Back
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were lower Tuesday morning, due to the mixed nature of the comparable oils.

Crude oil was a pinch higher, providing a little bit of spillover support to the vegetable oils. In Chicago, the soybeans were lower while the oil and meal notched small increases.

European rapeseed was pulling back but Malaysian palm oil was pushing upward.

Statistics Canada is set to issue its first crop production report Wednesday. Although record canola acres were planted this spring, given the varied conditions across the Prairies this growing season it's uncertain if there will be another record harvest or something less than the 21.81 million tonnes gleaned last year.

Last month Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada projected the canola harvest to be 21.6 million tonnes. The U.S. Department of Agriculture estimated the crop at 22.5 million tonnes.

Temperatures across the Prairies Tuesday are to be in the mid-teens Celsius, with rain expected for southern Alberta.

Canola crush margins increased with the November positions between C$272.90 to 283.70 per tonne above the futures.

The Canadian dollar eased back Tuesday morning with the loonie slipping to 71.81 U.S. cents, compared with Monday's close of 71.90.

About 14,800 contracts had been traded by 9:40 a.m. ET and prices in Canadian dollars per metric tonne were:

data.title: San Antonio is the Top Destination for Gen Z Movers — Market Talk
data.description: San Antonio is the most popular migration destination for Gen Zers, Redfin says. Houston is the hottest spot for millennial movers. Gen Zers are gravitating toward Washington, D.C. and Nashville--metros with plenty of job opportunities, along with lively social scenes. Millennials favor metro areas like Dallas and Baltimore--places that can offer more affordable housing. One thing the generations have in common: New York and Los Angeles are among the places they're most commonly leaving. Affordability is part of the story in pricey New York and Los Angeles, but Gen Z migration isn't purely about housing costs. Moves among young adults are also heavily influenced by college, first jobs and the transition from school into the workforce. (chris.wack@wsj.com)

data.title: Dollar Could Fall if Fed's Dot Plot Disappoints — Market Talk
data.description: The dollar could suffer some knee-jerk weakness if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates as expected but signals fewer future rate rises than markets anticipate Wednesday, TD Securities strategists say in a note. The Fed could lift rates by 25 basis points but this is largely priced in, they say. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh could cite higher-than-expected inflation as the motivation for potentially raising rates, they say. While he'll probably avoid forward guidance, the dot plot projections could show a median of two rate rises, they say. The DXY dollar index rises 0.2% to 99.566. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: Canada, EU to Begin Talks on 'Unique' Alliance Next Month, Carney Says — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira and Amanda Coletta

Canada and the European Union will begin talks next month on a new security and economic alliance, the latest bold step by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to reduce his country's economic reliance on the U.S.

Carney delivered the news Tuesday at an investment summit he's hosting in Toronto, where some of the world's biggest investors - from Wall Street heavyweights like Blackstone and BlackRock to sovereign-wealth funds from Norway and Abu Dhabi - are attending as the Canadian leader makes a pitch for their investment dollars.

Late Tuesday, Carney is traveling to Europe where he's set to deliver remarks to the European Parliament. In remarks at the summit, Carney provided a preview of what's ahead.

"Next month, we will begin discussions with the EU - the world's second-largest economy - to build a unique security and economic alliance," Carney said.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday that Carney instructed his special envoy to Europe to scope out the most ambitious possibilities short of full membership in the EU or its common market, according to people familiar with the matter. Canadian and European officials are discussing ways for Canada to informally lock into Europe's $20 trillion single market in key supply chains, the Journal reported.

A senior Canadian official said this week's trip, that also includes a stop in Liverpool for a meeting with U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, is meant to lay the groundwork for a EU-Canada summit in Montreal next month.

The move to seek a special alliance with the EU comes amid a sharp deterioration in trade ties between Ottawa and Washington. The two capitals are mired in a heightened trade conflict after talks on a tariff collapsed last month. Both countries have now imposed hefty tariffs on each other's exports.

Carney said that Canada would continue to be the U.S.'s most important partner in many key areas.

"These arrangements work when we engage as true partners that respect each other's traditions and sovereignty," he said. "When those opportunities return, Canada will be an even better partner-stronger, more resilient, more independent-ready to advance our mutual economic and security interests."

In a fireside-chat format after his speech, Carney said the global economy is in "a time when integration and sovereignty are in friction. For countries that want to retain sovereignty - and Canada wants to retain sovereignty for all the right reasons, including our unique culture - we need to use our assets to an advantage and pair with those that complement them."

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: September FOMC preview: possibility of rate hike, hawkish dot plot, divided Fed
data.description:
With a strong jobs report and a hotter-than-expected core CPI report for August, the Federal Open Market Committee is widely expected to raise its benchmark rate to 3.75%-4.00% from the current target range of 3.50%-3.75% at its September meeting.

"For the Fed, it might have been possible to read the August CPI report as glass half full if nothing else were in the news. The August PPI report released Thursday showed cool increases of healthcare services and portfolio management services, which mostly aren't in the CPI but are in the PCE index that the Fed uses for its two percent target," said Bill Adams, chief U.S. economist at Fifth Third Commercial Bank.

However, the energy price spike overshadows the August inflation reports, according to Adams. "Consumers may experience higher gas prices viscerally as they drive down the street, but core inflation is more vulnerable to diesel price shocks since businesses mainly use diesel to power their truck fleets."

"For the Fed, early September's surging energy prices will probably tip the scale to a hike," said the economist.

Goldman Sachs believes the FOMC will proceed with the hike primarily to avoid the negative market reaction that would likely follow if rates were kept on hold.

However, Michael Strain, director of economic policy studies and senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, said he does not believe a majority of the FOMC has materially changed its assessment since July, leading him to expect the central bank to leave rates unchanged this week.

Strain acknowledged that the August consumer price index report could have shifted some FOMC members toward favoring a rate increase, but argued that the data would have needed to be significantly more concerning to prompt the Fed to begin a new hiking cycle.

Strain believes most FOMC members could still view the data as consistent with ongoing disinflation rather than a meaningful reacceleration in inflation. The view points to a more divided Fed.

Currently, the probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at this week's meeting stands at 90.7%, compared with 9.3% odds of maintaining the target rate at 3.50% to 3.75%, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

If effective, the hike will be the Fed's first since July 2023 but unlikely to be the last for this year. A September hike could be the first in a cycle of monetary policy tightening, according to a report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

This week's meeting is Kevin Warsh's third heading the central bank.

Warsh has staunchly defended his view that the so-called "forward guidance", or signaling the likely direction of the FOMC's policy path, isn't useful.

So, the FOMC statement will likely only provide commentary on the current decision rather than insight into where rates are heading. Therefore, the Summary of Economic Projections, particularly the closely watched "dot plot", will be of significance.

Strategists at TD Securities expect the Fed to raise the policy rate three times in 2026, beginning in September. The previous forecast was that the central bank would hold rates during the year. The SEP projections should be hawkish.

Meanwhile, bond traders price in two hikes this year after the Consumer Price Index report, Bloomberg reported last week.

June dot plot showed the median federal funds rate landing at 3.8% at the end of 2026, compared to the March projection of 3.4%. The September dot plot could see the rate surpass 4.1%.

The question is, can rate hikes bring down inflation that is being driven by energy prices and the AI build-out? Addison Maier, portfolio manager at Janus Henderson Investors, told S&P Global Market Intelligence that hikes cannot impact the price of oil or the outcome of the conflict in Iran, nor change the trajectory of AI spending. However, higher rates could quicken the pace of decline in tariff-driven goods inflation and inflation in the housing sector.

data.title: ResMed upgraded at RBC Capital Markets on Q4 positives
data.description:
RBC Capital Markets on Tuesday upgraded ResMed to Outperform from Sector Perform and raised its price target to $262 from $244, citing positives in the respiratory device maker’s Q4 results for fiscal 2026.

Shares of ResMed fell in early August as investors reacted to its Q4 FY26 report, which, according to RBC analyst Craig Wong-Pan, included a large share buyback program for FY27 and was the first time the company issued revenue and earnings guidance.

Wong-Pan expects the San Diego, California-based MedTech to record high-single-digit earnings per share growth over the next three years despite a potential U.S. return of the rival Philips , which faced a recall of millions of respiratory devices in 2021.

The earnings report, which was also the first for ResMed’s new CFO, Aaron Bloomer, “marked a pivotal change in how the company will be fiscally managed,” wrote the analyst, adding that his upgrade was based on the company’s “positive earnings outlook and an undemanding valuation.”
